posts.title: Building the rooftop in clay
posts.excerpt: Chapter 15 opens on a roof at dusk, so I built one: forty tiles, one moon, two evenings.
posts.content:
Each tile is a flattened ball of grey clay pressed with the back of a spoon. The moon is a ping-pong ball with a torch inside.

With one lamp low on the left, the long shadows did the drawing for me. The screen tone follows the photo almost line for line.

posts.title: Find me at the Harbour Comic Fair
posts.excerpt: Table B-12 on 7 December, with a new print run of Lighthouse Road.
posts.content:
I will bring sixty copies, a few signed prints and the clay lighthouse itself, which survived the summer.

Come early if you want a sketch in your copy: I draw ten a day and then my hand needs tea.

posts.title: Why I still ink by hand
posts.excerpt: A dip pen wobbles. That wobble is the part readers remember.
posts.content:
A digital line is perfect every time, and it looks it. A G-pen gets thicker when I slow down and thinner when I am sure.

It takes longer, and a blot means starting the panel again. I still think it is worth it.
